title: Jenkins Reference
description: A quick reminder of the ideas and examples in the Jenkins lessons. Open the linked lesson when you need more help.

entries.name: Meet a pipeline
entries.summary: A pipeline is a saved sequence of build or check steps. Jenkins can run it and keep a record of the result.
notes: Jenkins is a separate automation tool; this learning app does not need a Jenkins server.

entries.name: Controllers and agents
entries.summary: The Jenkins controller coordinates work. An agent is an environment where jobs can execute.

example.code:
Controller: schedules and records jobs
Agent: runs the assigned build steps

notes: Do not give a build more access to the host machine than it needs.

entries.name: Stages show the journey
entries.summary: A stage groups related steps under a clear name. This helps people see where a run failed.
notes: Do not label a stage Test if it only prints a message; the example messages are demonstrations.

entries.name: Shell steps need the right agent
entries.summary: sh runs a shell command on a suitable Unix-like agent. Windows agents normally use a different step such as bat or powershell.
notes: Do not assume sh exists on every agent.

entries.name: Environment settings
entries.summary: An environment block provides named values to the pipeline. Use it for ordinary configuration, not hard-coded secrets.
notes: A value written in a Jenkinsfile is visible to people who can read that file.

entries.name: Parameters let a person choose
entries.summary: A parameter is an input supplied when a job is started. Treat input as data and validate it before using it.
notes: Never run arbitrary parameter text as a shell command.

entries.name: Conditions skip unneeded stages
entries.summary: when controls whether a stage runs. It lets a pipeline state a clear condition rather than hiding it inside many shell commands.
notes: Skipping a check should be visible and intentional.

entries.name: Always perform cleanup
entries.summary: A post block can run after the main stages. always is useful for cleanup or reporting whether the run passed or failed.
notes: Do not use a broad delete command as a generic cleanup step.

entries.name: Bound a long-running step
entries.summary: A timeout stops waiting after a chosen limit. It keeps stuck work from occupying an agent indefinitely.
notes: A timeout is a limit, not evidence that the work is correct.

entries.name: Parallel work needs independence
entries.summary: Parallel branches can run independent checks at the same time. They should not accidentally change the same temporary files.
notes: Parallel steps that share mutable files can interfere with each other.

entries.name: Credentials stay outside source
entries.summary: Jenkins can provide credentials through configured bindings. A job should request only what it needs and avoid printing secret values.

example.code:
Jenkinsfile: names an approved credential binding
Credential store: holds the secret
Step: uses it for the authorised job only

notes: Masking log output is not permission to expose secrets to untrusted code.

entries.name: Read results honestly
entries.summary: A Jenkins result reports the configured pipeline outcome. Useful reports explain what was actually checked and what still needs review.

example.code:
Stage Check: completed
Configured checks: formatting only
Not checked: browser interactions

notes: Do not confuse a successful demonstration echo with a real test suite.
